q.t: x and y are in direct proportion. When x = 4, y = 12. Find y when x = 7.
q.e: In direct proportion y/x stays the same: 12/4 = 3, so y = 3 × 7 = 21.

q.t: x and y are in inverse proportion. When x = 3, y = 8. Find y when x = 6.
q.e: In inverse proportion x × y stays the same: 3 × 8 = 24, so y = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Doubling x halves y.

q.t: 5 kg of rice costs ₹200. Find the cost of 8 kg (in ₹).
q.e: 1 kg costs ₹40, so 8 kg cost ₹320.

q.t: 6 workers finish a job in 10 days. How many days do 12 workers take?
q.e: The job needs 60 worker-days. Twice the workers take half the time.

q.t: For a fixed distance, speed and time taken are in:
q.e: speed × time = distance, which is fixed. If one doubles, the other halves.

q.t: The number of articles bought and their total cost are in:
q.e: Buy twice as many and you pay twice as much: cost ÷ number stays the same.

q.t: If x/y is always the same number, then x and y are in:
q.e: A constant ratio is the definition of direct proportion.

q.t: If x × y is always the same number, then x and y are in:
q.e: A constant product is the definition of inverse proportion.

q.t: 3 pens cost ₹45. Find the cost of 7 pens (in ₹).
q.e: 1 pen costs ₹15, so 7 cost ₹105.

q.t: 4 pipes fill a tank in 6 hours. How long do 8 such pipes take (in hours)?
q.e: 24 pipe-hours of filling are needed. 24 ÷ 8 = 3.

q.t: 35 workers build a wall in 24 days. How many days would 28 workers take?
On a map 1 cm represents 25 km. Two towns are 7.5 cm apart on the map. Find the real distance (in km).
q.e: Direct proportion: 7.5 × 25 = 187.5.

q.t: A 6 m pole casts a 15 m shadow. At the same time a tree casts a 25 m shadow. Find the height of the tree (in m).
q.e: Height/shadow is the same for both: 6/15 = h/25, so h = 10.

q.t: 8 taps fill a tank in 27 minutes. How long do 6 taps take (in minutes)?
q.e: 216 tap-minutes are needed. 216 ÷ 6 = 36.

q.t: x and y are in inverse proportion. When x = 10, y = 6. Find x when y = 15.
q.e: x × y = 60 always, so x = 60 ÷ 15 = 4.

q.t: At 50 km/h a journey takes 6 hours. What speed is needed to do it in 5 hours (in km/h)?
q.e: Distance = 300 km. 300 ÷ 5 = 60.

q.t: A stock of fodder lasts 12 cows for 20 days. How long does it last 15 cows (in days)?
q.e: 240 cow-days of fodder ÷ 15 cows = 16 days.

q.t: A 22.5 m iron rod weighs 85.5 kg. Find the weight of 6 m of the same rod (in kg).
q.e: 1 m weighs 85.5 ÷ 22.5 = 3.8 kg, so 6 m weigh 22.8 kg.

q.t: A fort has food for 1200 soldiers for 28 days. How long would it last 1400 soldiers (in days)?
q.e: 33,600 soldier-days ÷ 1400 = 24.

q.t: Rina types 540 words in 30 minutes. How many words does she type in 6 minutes?
q.e: 18 words a minute × 6 = 108.

q.t: A camp has food for 1200 people for 35 days. After 5 days, 300 more people arrive. How many more days does the food last?
q.e: Food left = 1200 × 30 = 36,000 person-days. For 1500 people: 24 days.

q.t: 6 oxen OR 8 cows can graze a field in 28 days. How long do 9 oxen and 2 cows take together (in days)?
q.e: 6 oxen eat like 8 cows, so 9 oxen = 12 cows. Total 14 cows: 8 × 28 ÷ 14 = 16.

q.t: 10 men working 8 hours a day finish a job in 12 days. How many days do 16 men working 6 hours a day take?
q.e: Job = 960 man-hours. 16 × 6 = 96 man-hours a day, so 10 days.

q.t: 5 workers earn ₹3750 in 6 days. How much do 8 workers earn in 9 days (in ₹)?
q.e: One worker earns 3750 ÷ 30 = ₹125 a day. 8 × 9 = 72 worker-days × 125 = 9000.

q.t: A wheel with 20 teeth drives a wheel with 50 teeth. The small wheel makes 150 turns. How many turns does the large wheel make?
q.e: The same number of teeth pass the meeting point: 20 × 150 = 50 × turns, so 60 turns. More teeth, fewer turns.

q.t: A pipe fills 3/5 of a cistern in 1 minute. How many more seconds does the rest take?
q.e: 3 fifths take 60 s, so 1 fifth takes 20 s and the remaining 2 fifths take 40 s.

q.t: A train runs at 108 km/h. How far does it go in 15 seconds (in m)?
24 men can finish a job in 12 days. After 4 days, 8 men leave. How many more days does the job take?
q.e: Work left = 24 × 8 = 192 man-days. With 16 men: 12 days.

q.t: A floor needs 45 m of carpet that is 1.2 m wide. How many metres are needed of carpet 1.5 m wide?
q.e: The area is fixed: 45 × 1.2 = 54 m². 54 ÷ 1.5 = 36 m. Wider carpet, shorter length.

q.t: 8 men OR 12 boys can do a job in 16 days. How long do 12 men and 6 boys take together (in days)?
q.e: 12 boys = 8 men, so 6 boys = 4 men. That makes 16 men: 8 × 16 ÷ 16 = 8 days.

q.t: 15 men working 8 hours a day finish a job in 21 days. 3 women do as much work as 2 men. How many days do 21 women working 6 hours a day take?
q.e: 21 women = 14 men. Job = 15 × 8 × 21 = 2520 man-hours. 14 × 6 = 84 man-hours a day → 30 days.

q.t: A garrison of 2000 men has food for 54 days. After 15 days, reinforcements arrive and the food lasts only 20 more days. How many men arrived?
q.e: Food left = 2000 × 39 = 78,000 man-days. For 20 days that feeds 3900 men, so 1900 arrived.

q.t: A works twice as fast as B. Together they finish a job in 14 days. How long would A take alone (in days)?
q.e: A does 2 parts a day for each 1 of B: together 3 parts. The job is 14 × 3 = 42 parts, and A alone does 2 a day: 21 days.

q.t: 12 men dig a 150 m trench in 5 days. How many days do 20 men take to dig a 300 m trench?
q.e: 150 m needs 60 man-days, so 300 m needs 120. With 20 men: 6 days.

q.t: x varies directly as y and inversely as z. x = 12 when y = 9 and z = 6. Find x when y = 15 and z = 10.
q.e: x = k × y/z. From the first set, k = 12 × 6 ÷ 9 = 8. Then x = 8 × 15 ÷ 10 = 12.

q.t: Travelling at 3/4 of its usual speed, a car arrives 20 minutes late. Find its usual journey time (in minutes).
q.e: At 3/4 the speed the time becomes 4/3 of usual. The extra 1/3 of the usual time is 20 minutes, so usual time = 60.

q.t: 5 machines make 5 parts in 5 minutes. How many minutes do 100 machines take to make 100 parts?
q.e: Each machine makes one part in 5 minutes. 100 machines each make one part — still 5 minutes.

q.t: 4 equal taps fill a tank in 9 hours. After 3 hours, 2 more such taps are opened. How many more hours does it take to fill the tank?
q.e: Job = 36 tap-hours; 12 are done. The remaining 24 are shared by 6 taps: 4 hours.

q.t: A train passes a pole in 12 seconds and a 200 m platform in 20 seconds. Find the length of the train (in m).
q.e: The extra 8 seconds are spent covering the 200 m platform: speed = 25 m/s. Length = 25 × 12 = 300 m.

q.t: A contractor must finish a road in 40 days and uses 30 men. After 25 days only half the work is done. How many extra men does he need?
q.e: Half the work took 30 × 25 = 750 man-days, so the other half needs 750 more in 15 days: 50 men. That is 20 extra.
